::: {.statx-chapter-banner}
## See how statistical estimators are built

This optional lab will turn abstract mathematical-statistics ideas into graphs, simulations, and interpretable estimation problems.
:::

## Learning objectives

By the end of this lab, students will be able to:

1. Construct and graph a likelihood function.
2. Locate and interpret a maximum-likelihood estimate.
3. Compare maximum-likelihood and maximum-a-posteriori estimates conceptually.
4. Investigate bias, variance, and large-sample behavior through simulation.

## Planned workflow

::: {.statx-topic-grid}
::: {.statx-topic-card}
### 1. Probability model

State the data-generating assumptions and identify the unknown parameter.
:::

::: {.statx-topic-card}
### 2. Likelihood curve

Evaluate plausible parameter values and visualize which are most compatible with the data.
:::

::: {.statx-topic-card}
### 3. MLE and MAP

Compare an estimate driven only by the observed data with one informed by a prior distribution.
:::

::: {.statx-topic-card}
### 4. Estimator behavior

Use repeated samples to study bias, variance, consistency, and approximation.
:::
:::

## Deliverables

- A clearly labeled likelihood plot
- A maximum-likelihood calculation
- A conceptual MLE-versus-MAP comparison
- A simulation study of estimator performance
